schema.description: Set true ONLY for a figure the user supplied for this factor, with its actual source; the host must verify that source before recording it as theirs. A verified retained human statement counts. Set false ONLY when explicitly proposing a new Olumi estimate now, with its own basis; for keep: true, false identifies the existing recorded Olumi estimate being retained. Never infer false from missing, truncated or unmatched source, or from the absence of a user-authorship claim. Do not use false to relabel an old quoted, copied or recorded figure. Keep the original statement, subject and qualifications separate from any new interpretation. This flag is a claim to check, not proof of authorship; accepting an Olumi estimate does not turn it into a user-supplied fact.

tool_description.before: Propose starting values for factors that have none, so the model can be reasoned about instead of sitting blank. This does NOT change anything: it records an exact proposal and returns its id, which you keep for authorise_change: show the user the values, never the id, before asking them to approve. Each value is an assumption for the user to adopt or correct, NEVER a measurement — say so; a value the result marks `your_figure` is the user’s own figure, never called an assumption. Propose only factors the model actually has, using the labels get_canonical_state returned. A factor that already holds a value is left alone UNLESS you set `revise: true` on it, which you may do ONLY when the user has just asked for that factor to be changed and named the number themselves. Never set it to replace someone’s figure with one of your own. When the user asks to revise an existing value without supplying a replacement figure, ask what figure they would use; never supply a number or an instruction for them to repeat as their own. When the user says Olumi’s current estimate for a factor is right and should stay, set `keep: true` on it instead: nothing changes, and their approval records that they accepted Olumi’s estimate.
tool_description.after: Propose starting values for factors that have none, so the model can be reasoned about instead of sitting blank. This does not change anything: it records an exact proposal and returns its id for authorise_change. Show the complete approval card with every proposed value, its unit, source, basis and qualifications, and any omitted or unsupported parts; never show the id as consent. Supply the required user_stated boolean for every item: true identifies a user-supplied figure whose source must verify; false explicitly proposes a new Olumi estimate with its own basis, or identifies an existing recorded Olumi estimate when keep is true. Missing or unverifiable source is unknown, not evidence of a new AI estimate. Preserve verified human origin, known unknown source and the original words separately from a new interpretation; approval adopts an estimate without changing its original authorship. An Olumi estimate is an assumption to adopt or correct, never a measurement; a value the result marks your_figure is the user's own figure and must not be called an Olumi assumption. Propose only factors the model actually has, using the labels returned by get_canonical_state. A factor that already holds a value is left alone unless revise is true, which is allowed only when the user has just requested that factor's change and supplied the replacement figure. Never replace someone's figure with one of your own under revise. When the user requests a revision without a replacement figure, ask what figure they would use; never supply a number or an instruction for them to repeat as their own. When the user says the current recorded Olumi estimate should stay, use keep: true instead: the value does not change, and approval records acceptance of Olumi's estimate. Keep and revise retain their existing separate approval and permission checks.

implementation_scope: Replace the existing description once; add the required boolean to the existing items schema/type and validate actual callers. No new response format/store/writer/parser/API or model call. Existing verified/tier-2 protections, whole-card, current revision/permission, native units and omission disclosures remain. False marks an explicit proposal act; it does not bypass known unknown source or retroactively erase original source. Keep:true retains canonical AI origin, not a new estimate.
proof_limit: Exact text/schema design support, not code/CI/provider/serving acceptance. Existing operator/checker proves actual assembled tool/context and human-positive/new-AI/unknown or missing/source-contradiction controls; no new study/scorer/gold change.
